registrar_rulings.reason: Approved as a genuinely new id: no id in any of the three namespaces prices raw chicken tenderloin, and the estate says so deliberately rather than by silence - chicken-breast's exclude list carries both 'tender' and 'strip' (commodities.json ~line 20-21), whole-chicken excludes 'tender' (~line 5206), and cooked-shredded-chicken excludes 'tenders?' (~line 66494), so three neighboring chicken ids all push tenderloin products AWAY on purpose; chicken-nuggets includes only 'chicken nuggets?' (breaded frozen, a different form). The live feed's only 'tenderloin' strings are pork-tenderloin (Sam's whole pork tenderloins) - 'chicken tender' appears nowhere priced, so this is unpriced as well as unminted. recipe-floor-id-map.json declares no pair for it. Same food as chicken-breast but a different cut on its own tray at a different per-lb price, the same distinction the estate already draws for thigh vs breast, so reuse of chicken-breast ($1.99/lb) would misprice ~5 lb of protein. FOLLOW-UP EDITS the caller must make via the sanctioned editors: (1) mint in the recipe namespace (recipe-board-everyday baseline + recipe-commodities.json so it can go on sale) unless Brad promotes it to weekly staples; (2) include patterns must be contiguous real-product phrases: 'chicken\s+(?:breast\s+)?tenderloins?' and 'tenderloins?\b.{0,15}\bchicken' - do NOT include bare 'tenders?', which is the breaded/prepared aisle; (3) excludes at neighboring-commodity rigor (chicken-breast's list is the template): breaded, battered, frozen, cooked, popcorn, crispy, dipp, glazed, sauced, nugget, patt, strip, pork, turkey, meal/entree, pet food, plus the beverage/supplement block every chicken id carries; (4) add commodity-dupe-allowlist.json pairs chicken-tenderloins|chicken-breast (same food different cut/tray) and chicken-tenderloins|pork-tenderloin (shared 'tenderloin' stem, different animal) so the daily audit never pages Brad on either; (5) a separate vocabulary answer per the two-namespace rule: db\ingredients.json has no 'Chicken Tenderloin' row yet - that name needs its own vocabulary minting through the food-DB gate, and this id ruling does not create it.
